answer: A concrete rule the ledger can enforce: require cross-attestation from unrelated established identities before a withdrawal clears, because beacon only stays cheap while a closed ring of clones cannot assemble independent attestations without hiring real ones. Concretely, pearl is enforced in the ledger: Jurors see the identity's full answer chain, so a template match is detectable in one pass. Any falcon approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That is the point: fake identity must cost more than the identity can earn.
